A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same function-vector framework and research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite the expanded scope and changed title.

before.justification: v1 reports original OpenFlamingo experiments on synthetic images and GQA, including intervention accuracy, ablations, fine-tuning, and analogy results.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for OpenFlamingo and Qwen3-VL, including agentic relations, unseen objects, cross-dataset transfer, and representation similarity.

M1.justification: The procedure remains causal head selection, aggregation of head activations, last-token vector injection, vector-only fine-tuning, and probability-weighted composition. Qwen3-VL supplies another experimental backbone; the revised explanations do not establish a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds GQA Agentic tasks covering carrying, holding, riding, sitting on, and wearing. It also evaluates ten held-out object identities and synthetic-to-GQA transfer. The original spatial relations and diagonal-relation analogy tasks remain.

E2.justification: The analogy comparison changes from one-, four-, and ten-shot ICL in v1 to zero-, one-, and four-shot baselines in v2. The standard relation experiments retain the zero-shot, four-shot, initial-FV, and fine-tuned-FV comparison structure.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct and expands GQA Spatial from 201 to 4,226 images, with tasks per relation increasing from 200 to 1,000. The stated fine-tuning schedule changes from 20 epochs at learning rate 0.001 to 10 epochs at 0.003. These are reported setting changes, not proof that every retained result was rerun. Agentic test size is inconsistent: Section 4.3 says 1,413 images, while Appendix A.2 specifies 706.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained injection-layer, head-count, and context-size ablations, v2 tests generalization to unseen objects, transfer from synthetic to real images, and cross-model relational geometry through RSA. These directly examine object dependence, domain dependence, and representation similarity.

E5.justification: Appendix G adds statistical comparison through RSA correlation estimates between models, absent from v1. This is a limited statistical-analysis addition; neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial Qwen3-VL, agentic, unseen-object, transfer, and RSA results. For example, Qwen3-VL CFV accuracy is reported as 45.1% versus 28.7% for four-shot ICL; these are newly reported conditions, not improvements over the same v1 setting. Some entries are inconsistent: v2 retains 16.8% for OpenFlamingo CFV in Section 4.4, but Figure 7 plots approximately 15%.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same activation averages, vector construction, additive intervention, training objective, and composition weights. Notation and explanations change, but no substantive mathematical derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the contribution from spatial relations in OpenFlamingo to visual relations across OpenFlamingo and Qwen3-VL, including agentic relations. The underlying claims about extraction, fine-tuning, and composition remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new tests as evidence of object-independent and cross-domain relational representations, while RSA indicates different relational geometries across models. It removes the single-architecture limitation and adds an explicit limitation that CFVs require a contextual source example, discussing weaker or noisier context as future work.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an explicit GitHub code address, a Qwen checkpoint, object-recognition screening details, and revised dataset and training specifications. The anonymous-OSF code-and-data reproducibility statement is removed; the new access statement explicitly promises code rather than all datasets. Resource availability was not externally checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds LLaVA and Qwen-family references and removes the separate CLIP and RedPajama references. Positioning relative to function vectors, visual task vectors, and multimodal mechanistic interpretability remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and terminology broaden, method paragraphs receive targeted rewrites, and the one-shot rationale is expanded. Appendices are reorganized, and an Impact Statement replaces the former closing disclosures. The main section sequence and method subsection organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The main paper adopts a two-column layout and substantially reorganizes its displays. Dataset examples are separated from results, main performance figures emphasize cross-model averages, and detailed results move to the appendix. New ICL and similarity tables and agentic and transfer plots accompany retained or resized diagrams and ablations.

improvement.justification: The second architecture, agentic tasks, and unseen-object and cross-dataset tests substantially address v1's explicit limitations in architectural and relational generality. They strengthen evidence that function vectors transfer beyond the original controlled setting. Reporting problems temper the gains: agentic split counts conflict, the OpenFlamingo analogy plot disagrees with its text, and Figure 15 does not support uniformly superior fine-tuned performance. These weaknesses limit precision but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in evidential coverage.
